fields.title: Storage
fields.description: Where documents live, and the rules Mortar applies whichever store you use.

data.title: Server functions belong in your app
data.body: The Solid Vite plugin compiles `'use server'` only outside `node_modules`, so Mortar exports plain functions and your app re-exports them from its own server-function module. `createContentServer` builds them for you: see below.

data.source:
## Several processes

Writes are serialized within one `createContent`. If several server processes share a store, the store itself needs to lock.

Want to keep content somewhere else? See [Writing a store](/docs/writing-a-store). Uploaded files have a store of their own: see [Assets](/docs/assets).

## Starter content

`seed(content, docs)` saves starter documents into collections that are still empty, through `createContent`, so they're validated like an editor's saves. Collections that already have documents are left alone, so it's safe to call every time the server starts. It works with any store, a database as well as the JSON files.

```ts
await seed(content, {
  categories: [{ id: 'news', slug: 'news', fields: { name: 'News' } }],
  pages: [{ id: 'home', slug: 'home', fields: { title: 'Welcome' }, entries: [] }],
});
```

Collections are filled in the order given, so a reference can point at a document seeded before it. Leave out `id` and a random one is made. A document that doesn't validate throws, naming it and its problems. With the JSON-file store you can also just commit the files: they are the seed.
